Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.cli

Class MandelaCli

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.mandela.cli.MandelaCli
public final class MandelaCli extends Object
The mandela command: run a program, check one, evaluate a one-liner, start a session, look at the instructions.

The CLI is a thin shell over Runtime — it owns no language behaviour of its own, which is the only way the two stay honest with each other. What it does own is the two decisions a command line has to make and a library must not: what the script is allowed to do, and what came out of the run.

The sandbox decision

mandela run FILE gives the program the desktop shape: it may print, and it may read and write files under the directory its own file sits in — nothing else. It gets no environment, no network, no process and no JVM, because a script author asking for println has not asked for those, and a language that hands them out silently is a language whose sandbox nobody can reason about. --sandbox DIR moves the root, and --unrestricted is the documented way to say "this script is mine and I want it to have the host's rights". The flag is loud on purpose.

Exit codes

Fixed, so a build script or a desktop launcher can branch on them without parsing prose: 0 the program ran, 1 the command line was wrong, 2 the program failed, 3 a file could not be read, 4 check found blocking problems. A compile error is a program failure (2), not a usage error (1): the author of mandela run broken.mnd gets the same code whether the mistake is a missing brace or a division by zero, which is what a Makefile expects.

    • execute

      public static int execute(String[] argv, BufferedReader in, PrintWriter out, PrintWriter err)
      Runs one command line, writing where it is told to.

      Separated from main(java.lang.String[]) and given the streams as arguments because a test and the desktop's own launcher both need the behaviour without a System.exit: the desktop embeds this class to offer a Mandela console panel, and a panel that killed the JVM when the user typed about would be a poor panel.

      Parameters:
      argv - the arguments, without the program name
      in - the console input, used by repl
      out - the standard output
      err - the standard error, where every failure is reported
      Returns:
      the process exit code, one of the constants above
